title.narrative: Output 6.1. Increased capacity of Member States to promote investments in the care economy and a more balanced sharing of family responsibilities

description.narrative: An action plan was introduced to promote equal opportunity in the world of work, in alignment with ILO conventions C183 and C156. The plan focused on enhancing policies and legislation while providing quality childcare services to support increased women's labour force participation in the care sector and improve work conditions in this domain. As part of this initiative, a model for childcare cooperatives will be established based on recommendations of a comprehensive assessment of the childcare nurseries sector in the Occupied Palestinian Territory, and the landscape assessment for childcare cooperatives in OPT, which was conducted to check out the feasibility of modelling the provision of childcare services through cooperatives. Based on the childcare cooperatives landscape assessment findings, a feasible model for childcare cooperatives was developed and national training modules were introduced promoting professionalism in the care sector. In its commitment to promoting policies that reduce work-family conflict and address labour market discrimination arising from family responsibilities, in accordance with the ILO convention No. 156 on "Workers with Family Responsibilities," the ILO has played a pivotal role in advancing childcare services in the Occupied Palestinian Territory (OPT). Through conducting a thorough assessment of the childcare nurseries sector, the ILO undertook a comprehensive analysis, combining quantitative and qualitative methodologies to evaluate its impact on equal opportunities in the workforce. To ensure the accuracy and relevance of the results, the ILO facilitated validation discussions with social partners. Furthermore, the ILO has undertaken an evaluation of the landscape of cooperatives in the OPT, aiming to explore the feasibility of establishing affordable and high-quality childcare services through cooperatives to support economic opportunities for women. The assessment recommended sector-based cooperatives as the most suitable model for delivering childcare services in the OPT context. This model is anticipated to offer a promising, cost-effective, and high-quality childcare option, aligning with the ILO's commitment to fostering inclusive and supportive work environments. Furthermore, the ILO actively and with support from the Care COOP Unit contributed to the development of the childcare cooperative model by providing the required expertise and guidance to conduct feasibility assessments and creating business plans and model based on international best practices. Additionally, specialists provided by the ILO will formulate training modules and secured their accreditation, supporting the capacity building of childcare providers.

Output 6.3. Increased capacity of Member States to develop gender-responsive legislation, policies and measures for a world of work free from violence and harassment

description.narrative:
To strengthen workers’ protection against violence and harassment atwork, the Palestinian General Federation of Trade Unions (PGFTU), with the support of the ILO, succeeded in signing 4 collective bargaining agreements between sectoral trade unions and private of companies. These agreements cover 7658 of workers and aim at improving working conditions, particularly for women workers. The agreements contain among other things, provision of a complaints mechanism for reporting cases of violence and harassment, referral system for victims, including legal and psychological support. Action against violence and harassment in the private sector was also strengthened by the signing of 22 codes of conduct at private enterprises. These codes of conduct outline practical guidelines and procedures on addressing violence and harassment at work in a written policy document that sets the standard of behaviour for all parties. To strengthen access to justice mechanisms for victims of violence and harassment, the PGFTU with the support of the ILO, launched a complaints unit system aimed at receiving and documenting workplace violations and complaints, with focus on cases of violence and harassment. This system consists of 14 complaint units (CU) spread across the West Bank, managed by 14 women trade unionists. Since its launch in March of 2022, the complaints system specifically designed database registered a total of 163 complaints until July 2023, covering violations in workplace safety and health arrangements, poor working conditions including payment of wages below the minimum wage, unpaid leaves, and gender-based violence (GBV). To enhance regulatory and legislative protections against violence and harassment, law reforms to include provisions on violence and harassment in the world of work in legislation is underway in the OPT. The draft law contains new provisions on preventing violence and harassment and is in the process of endorsement by the authorities.
a) The ILO has empowered women trade unionists through comprehensive training on ILO's Convention 190 on Violence and Harassment, along with mediation skills. Additionally, the ILO has provided training on Alternative Dispute Resolution mechanisms, enhancing their capacity to address workplace disputes effectively. Moreover, the ILO has facilitated the assessment and revision of the complaints units' structure by engaging a legal consultant to evaluate its functions and referral mechanisms and make recommendations for its improvement ensuring continuous advancement and efficiency. b) The ILO has provided the PGFTU with technical inputs have been vital in finalizing the codes of conduct for various firms, reinforcing a culture of respect and equality in the workplace. Moreover, capacity-building initiatives provided by the ILO have empowered these firms by establishing workplace complaint committees and channels for reporting workplace complaints. c) The ILO has actively contributed to Birzeit University's efforts to promote gender equality and social justice through technical inputs and support in revising the code of conduct and formulating bylaws for the establishment of the Observatory for Gender and Social Justice. By collaborating closely with the university, the ILO has helped enhance the effectiveness of the code of conduct, ensuring it aligns with international labour standards and promotes an inclusive and equitable campus environment. d) Through policy support and technical inputs, the ILO has played a pivotal role in facilitating the revision process of the Labour Law, aligning it with global labour best practices. Additionally, the ILO has provided essential capacity-building initiatives to the Ministry of Labour, enhancing their capabilities to manage and address complaints through a robust and effective mechanism.
